data.title: Microsoft stock steadies after global outage as AI competition intensifies
data.description:
Microsoft shares recovered on Friday after a global outage disrupted its Outlook, Teams and Copilot services, affecting users across more than 70 countries.

The incident has renewed concerns about businesses' dependence on centralised cloud services, while intensifying competition in artificial intelligence adds to the pressure on the technology giant.

Microsoft apologises as outage disrupts services

Microsoft shares MSFT rose approximately 0.18% to $523.94 on Friday, recovering from a decline of more than 2% in premarket trading.

The outage, which began on Thursday, November 12, affected several Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook email, Teams and the Copilot AI assistant.

According to Downdetector, users across more than 70 countries reported disruptions.

The incident affected services used by more than 430 million people, alongside governments and organisations worldwide.

Microsoft engineers worked for more than 20 hours to address the disruption.

In its latest updates, Microsoft apologised for the outage, saying it was "deeply sorry" for the disruption caused since Thursday.

In a 3:05 p.m. EST update, the company said it did not yet have a timeline for full recovery.

Earlier, Microsoft had said it was seeing "broad recovery and stability" across its services.

"Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration," the company said in an earlier update.

Microsoft also dismissed speculation that the outage was linked to technical issues involving artificial intelligence agents.

It said the incident was caused by a technical issue and was not related to cybersecurity or AI agents.

The company plans to publish a full post-incident report after completing its review.

Outage highlights dependence on cloud services

The disruption has drawn attention to the risks associated with businesses relying heavily on a small number of major technology providers.

Microsoft's cloud-based model allows organisations to avoid the costs of operating and maintaining their own email servers and infrastructure.

However, a prolonged outage at a major provider can affect large numbers of businesses simultaneously.

Microsoft's second-quarter availability for its Microsoft 365 workplace applications was reported at 99.994% globally, making prolonged disruptions relatively rare.

Nevertheless, the incident could encourage companies to invest more in backup services and continuity arrangements.

Providers such as US cybersecurity firm Mimecast offer continuity services that allow users to send and receive emails through temporary inboxes when their primary systems become unavailable.

Privacy-focused technology company Proton also offers standby email accounts that businesses can activate during disruptions.

According to a study by Oxford Economics and Splunk, unplanned outages of critical digital business systems cost Global 2000 companies an average of $15,000 per minute.

While continuity services have traditionally attracted deadline-sensitive industries such as law, the latest disruption could encourage wider adoption among accounting firms, hospitals and other regulated businesses.

Geopolitical tensions have also increased concerns about dependence on US technology providers, particularly in Europe.

The outage highlighted how technical failures alone can disrupt access to essential digital services.

AI competition adds to pressure on Microsoft

The outage comes at a challenging time for Microsoft as investors assess its position in the artificial intelligence market.

Recent reports about OpenAI's latest figures have raised questions about its competitive position relative to Anthropic.

Microsoft owns a 24% stake in OpenAI and has a smaller investment in Anthropic.

Anthropic also recently introduced a new suite of office tools, adding to competition in a market where Microsoft has a significant presence through its productivity software and Copilot assistant.

Investors will be watching Microsoft's upcoming Ignite conference for updates on its AI strategy and cloud platform Azure.

Citi analyst Tyler Radke said the event could reinforce confidence in the company's AI growth outlook.

"We expect the event to reinforce confidence in Microsoft's AI growth narrative," Radke said in a research note.

The conference could provide investors with further insight into Microsoft's cloud and Copilot developments as the company seeks to maintain its position in an increasingly competitive AI market.

data.title: Why SpaceX shares are sliding ahead of historic Starship Flight 15 launch?
data.description:
SpaceX SPCX shares fell on Friday ahead of a high-stakes Starship test flight, with investors also weighing growing scrutiny of Elon Musk's potential merger plans involving Tesla.

The stock traded 1% lower on Friday at around 11:45 AM EDT.

Major US indexes also moved lower, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq shedding over 1.6% as investors continued to digest headlines around outgoing Nvidia chief Jensen Huang

Tesla merger faces growing political scrutiny

One factor weighing on SpaceX was increased scrutiny of its potential merger with Tesla.

Bloomberg reported on Thursday that the companies could announce a deal as soon as December.

However, the changing political environment could bring greater scrutiny to merger discussions involving two of the state's most valuable companies.

At the federal level, Democrats who took control of Congress have signaled plans to investigate Musk's business and political activities.

Texas Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson has vowed to take a close look at the potential merger.

"Any merger of companies of that consequence warrants tremendous scrutiny," Johnson told Bloomberg.

He also raised concerns about the concentration of private and public-sector influence around Musk.

"I don't want anybody to have such control of the public sector that they can bend public power to their private gain. I think his Empire is at great risk of crossing that line," Johnson said of Musk.

However, Johnson also indicated a willingness to have discussions with the world's richest man, who donated heavily, but in vain, to Republican causes during the midterm elections.

Analysts have also highlighted structural obstacles to combining the two companies, particularly the challenge of separating Tesla's substantial Chinese manufacturing operations from SpaceX's sensitive US defense contracts.

SpaceX restructures Grok Imagine team

Separately, SpaceX's AI division laid off roughly 60 employees from the Grok Imagine video-generation team, The Information reported on Friday.

The cuts leave only a small number of employees to maintain the image and video features of the Grok chatbot.

They form part of a restructuring following the earlier integration of xAI into SpaceX.

The move reflects a shift in resources toward coding tools and other priorities, while adding to questions about the future development of Grok's image and video-generation capabilities.

Starship Flight 15 becomes another major catalyst

Investors are also focused on Starship Flight 15, which is set to take place later on Friday.

The mission aims to achieve a historic recovery of both the Super Heavy booster and the upper-stage Starship using the launch tower's mechanical arms.

A successful recovery would mark an important advance in SpaceX's efforts to develop a rapidly reusable launch system.

It could also support denser Starlink deployments and the company's longer-term ambitions involving orbital computing infrastructure.

KeyBanc on Friday reiterated its Sector Weight rating on SpaceX, while expressing optimism about the upcoming Starship launch.

"The launch is a key milestone for the program, as SPCX seeks to demonstrate fixes and enhancements implemented following some anomalies encountered during Flight 14 in September 2026," the brokerage said.

Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas also reiterated an Overweight rating on SpaceX, maintaining his $300 price target.

Jonas described a successful catch of the Starship and Super Heavy booster as "one of the most significant potential catalysts in SpaceX's nearly 25-year history."

The upcoming flight therefore represents an important milestone for the company as it works to demonstrate the improvements made following Flight 14 and advance its reusable rocket program.

data.title: Broadcom stock falls 6% as this firm flags AI financing risks
data.description:
Broadcom shares AVGO fell more than 6% on Friday after Rothschild & Co Redburn downgraded the semiconductor company, citing concerns about its growing exposure to artificial intelligence financing arrangements.

The investment firm lowered its rating on Broadcom to Neutral from Buy and cut its price target by 33%, from $595 to $398.

The downgrade comes after Broadcom shares rallied over the previous five trading sessions as investors looked beyond Nvidia's leadership turmoil and considered the potential benefits for rival chipmakers.

However, Rothschild & Co Redburn believes the optimism surrounding Broadcom's potential market share gains may be premature, particularly as questions remain about its exposure to AI infrastructure financing.

Redburn flags Broadcom's $43 billion AI financing exposure

One of the firm's primary concerns is Broadcom's backstop arrangement for Anthropic's rack leases.

Under the arrangement, Broadcom's maximum potential liability could reach approximately $43 billion.

Analysts at Rothschild & Co Redburn argued that this creates meaningful financial risks if Anthropic or other frontier AI laboratory customers fail to become financially self-sufficient.

The exposure has become an important consideration as investors assess the financial commitments associated with the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure.

The firm also highlighted uncertainty surrounding Google's efforts to develop customer-owned tooling.

“Beyond this, the market needs reassurance that Google’s customer-owned tooling efforts will not become widespread,” Rothschild & Co Redburn said.

The firm believes Broadcom could still benefit if these concerns are addressed. However, it expects the process to take time.

“The upside potential to Broadcom shares from clearing these hurdles is appreciable but is unlikely to occur quickly,” the analysts wrote.

The firm added that this limits the potential for Broadcom's valuation to rise relative to its peers in the near term, prompting the downgrade to Neutral.

Nvidia turmoil had supported Broadcom shares

The downgrade followed a strong rally in Broadcom shares over the previous five sessions.

Investors had been rotating away from Nvidia following the resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang amid controversy surrounding his personal relationships.

The leadership change prompted speculation that cloud providers and other large technology companies could accelerate their efforts to develop custom AI chips.

Broadcom has been viewed as a potential beneficiary of this trend, given its position in the custom chip market.

However, Rothschild & Co Redburn argued that the anticipated shift in market share remains largely sentiment-driven rather than evidence of a confirmed structural change.

The firm also suggested that the potential benefits may take longer to materialise than investors currently expect.

Wall Street remains broadly bullish on Broadcom

Despite the downgrade, the broader analyst outlook for Broadcom remains positive.

According to TipRanks data, 29 of the 31 analysts covering the company have assigned it a Buy rating.

While analysts remain optimistic about the company's position in the expanding AI chip market, financing commitments and uncertainty around customer-owned technology could influence its valuation.

data.title: Cisco earnings were strong: why is the stock sliding then?
data.description:
Cisco Systems (CSCO) posted the kind of earnings report that usually sends investors reaching for the buy button.

Revenue came in at $18.5 billion, and earnings soared to $1.4 per share – up more than expected, 24% and 40% versus the same quarter last year.

Yet, Cisco stock opened in the red this morning.

The disconnect reflects a tougher question facing the networking giant: how much should investors pay for its AI expansion when margins are shrinking and order growth is losing speed?

Cisco stock sinks on a profitability trade-off

The first concern sits between Cisco’s sales and its bottom line. Adjusted gross margin dropped to 65.6% from 68.1% a year earlier.

Management attributed the squeeze to hardware growing faster than software and services, alongside elevated memory costs.

That matters because selling more equipment can produce impressive revenue growth while leaving CSCO with less gross profit from each sales dollar.

However, describing this as an earnings-quality collapse would go too far. Adjusted operating expenses increased just 2%, helping Cisco achieve a record 37.8% adjusted operating margin.

CSCO shares are under pressure primarily because of the durability concern.

Cost discipline is cushioning the changing sales mix today.

Sustaining that protection becomes harder if hiring, investment, or other expenses eventually accelerate.

Shareholders therefore need to watch both margins, rather than treating either one as the complete profitability story.

Strong orders leave investors questioning the pace

The second sticking point is the direction of demand.

Product orders increased 21% from a year earlier, a healthy result but slower than the preceding quarter’s 35% growth.

That made several Wall Street analysts reduce their price targets on Cisco shares after earnings, highlighting potential growth deceleration and tougher comparisons in campus networking.

Orders matter because they help investors assess future business, while reported revenue largely describes equipment and services already delivered.

A slowdown in bookings growth can therefore overshadow an acceleration in current sales.

Still, slower growth does not mean shrinking demand.

Cisco’s earnings call showed enterprise orders rising 15% and public-sector orders increasing 13%, suggesting spending strength extends beyond the biggest cloud operators.

The unresolved issue is whether those customers can sustain momentum as comparisons become more demanding.

Should you buy the dip in CSCO stock?

Cisco’s revised outlook gives investors a substantial counterargument to the selling.

Management now projects fiscal 2027 revenue of $74.8 billion at least and adjusted earnings of $5.47 to $5.53 per share.

It also expects $9 billion in AI infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers, more than twice the previous fiscal year’s total.

The forecast supports a growing business, but they do not automatically establish that CSCO stock is cheap.

The stronger investment case would combine continued order expansion with evidence that the hardware-heavy sales mix can support lasting profit growth.

Friday’s reaction suggests investors want that evidence before rewarding Cisco with a higher valuation.

data.title: Trump Media stock jumped after earnings: beware of key risks
data.description:
Trump Media stock bounced back this week after the company announced its financial results, which showed strong revenue and profitability growth. DJT jumped to $5, up by over 40% from its lowest point this month. Still, the company faces some major risks as Bitcoin falls and as Democrats prepares to take power.

Trump Media stock jumps after earnings

Trump Media, the parent company of Truth Social, published its third-quarter report, which provided insights about its business. The results showed that the company’s revenue jumped by 205% in the third quarter to $3 million. This revenue was driven by Truth API, the newly launched service that gives users the ability to pay for early access of Trump’s social media posts.

Most notably, the company said that its profit jumped during the quarter. It jumped to $409.7 million in the third quarter, much higher than the losses it generated in the same period last year. 

However, the reality is that these growth catalysts face some major risks ahead. First, Democrats won the midterm elections by a large margin. They are on track to win 56 seats in the Senate and more than 250 in the House of Representatives. Since corruption was one of the biggest issues in this election, Democrats will likely probe Trump Media for the Truth API solution.

Critics argue that the company is engaging in illegalities by allowing Trump to benefit from his social media posts. In other words, he is allowing rich high-frequency trading companies to have market-moving information before the rest of the market.

The other crucial risk that Trump Media faces is the ongoing Bitcoin price weakness. Bitcoin plunged to $67,700, down by over 22% from its highest point in September this year. It has moved to its lowest level since August 20th this year. 

The ongoing Bitcoin weakness is important for Trump Media because it is one of the biggest holders. It holds 15,649 coins, making it the 9th-largest Bitcoin holder in the world. Its Bitcoin holdings explain why its profit jumped in the third quarter as the coin jumped from $57,700 to $126,300 in October.

Further, the decision to merge with TAE Technologies faces risks since the company is not yet profitable. It was established in 1998 and has spent this period researching on its technology. While it has made substantial progress in this period, it is still unclear whether it will become a profitable company in the long term. 

Meanwhile, data compiled by SimilarWeb shows that Truth Social is not a popular social media platform. Its website visitors dropped by 22% in October from September. It has dropped by over 50% from a year earlier, a trend that has accelerated as Trump’s approval rating plunged. This trend will continue after the last midterm election in which the Republican party lost big.

DJT stock price technical analysis

Trump Media stock chart | Source: TradingView

The daily chart shows that the Trump Media stock has been in a strong freefall this year and is now hovering near its all-time low. It has remained below the important support level of $6.85, its lowest level on June 26. 

The stock has remained below the 50-day and 100-day moving averages and the Supertrend indicators. Also, there is a risk that the ongoing rebound is a dead-cat bounce, a temporary rebound that is often followed by a retreat.

Therefore, the stock will likely resume the downward trend, and retest the support level of $3.7, its lowest level this week. A move below that level will point to more downside, potentially to the psychological level of $3.0.

data.title: Evening digest: oil heads for weekly decline, Tesla SpaceX merger talks advance
data.description:
Oil prices edged higher on Friday as signs of a growing global supply surplus and easing concerns over further military escalation in the Middle East weighed on the market.

Meanwhile, US producer inflation rose less than expected in October, although persistent price pressures continued to complicate the Federal Reserve's policy outlook.

Oil prices head for second weekly decline

Oil prices gained on Friday; however, Brent and West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude are on track for a second consecutive weekly decline.

Brent futures fell 0.13% to $95.94 a barrel, while WTI declined 0.09% to $88.81.

Both benchmarks were set to lose around 2% for the week, following declines of 16% and 13%, respectively, in the previous week.

The market has shifted from concerns about supply shortages to fears of a potential surplus.

An International Energy Agency report released on Friday pointed to an increase in the global oil surplus, while lower geopolitical risks also weighed on prices.

US crude and fuel inventories also increased last week, reflecting softer demand for refined products and higher oil imports, according to the Energy Information Administration.

However, risks to shipments through the Strait of Hormuz remain.

Iran's military said four oil tankers were hit by explosions in the waterway on Thursday, while Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure.

US PPI rises less than expected in October

US wholesale prices increased 0.3% in October, below the 0.4% forecast by economists surveyed by Dow Jones, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.

Core PPI, which excludes food and energy, also rose 0.3%, in line with expectations.

However, the annual headline rate accelerated to 6.5%, its highest level since November 2022.

Goods prices were a major contributor to the increase.

Final demand goods prices rose 0.5% during the month, while the goods index increased 10.2% year over year, its largest annual gain since October 2022.

Services prices rose 0.2%, with transportation and warehousing contributing to the increase. Truck freight transportation prices climbed 3.9%.

The figures offered some relief after consumer inflation also came in hotter than expected earlier in the week.

However, the annual acceleration in producer prices and broader cost pressures could complicate the Fed's next decision.

Markets were pricing in a December rate increase, with the CME FedWatch tool showing an 87.7% probability of a 25-basis-point hike and a 12.3% chance of a 50-basis-point move.

Gold struggles despite softer PPI reading

Gold prices fell on Friday after the producer inflation report came in below expectations.

However, the modest recovery did little to offset the previous session's steep losses.

Spot gold fell 0.03% to $3,875.14 an ounce, after briefly reaching $3,922.97 following the PPI release. US gold futures for December delivery fell 0.14% to 3,880.10.

Bullion fell 3% on Thursday, reaching a more-than-one-year low as higher oil prices and hotter-than-expected consumer inflation strengthened concerns about interest rates remaining elevated.

Gold was down around 4.5% for the week, putting it on course for its worst weekly performance since early June.

Higher interest rates tend to reduce the appeal of non-yielding assets such as gold. Silver and platinum also declined on Friday, while palladium advanced.

Tesla and SpaceX merger talks gather pace

Tesla and SpaceX could announce a merger as soon as December, according to a Bloomberg report published on Thursday.

The potential deal would combine Tesla's electric vehicles, energy storage and robotics businesses with SpaceX's rockets, satellites and artificial intelligence operations.

Based on their valuations of more than $1.9 trillion and around $1.5 trillion, respectively, the combined company could be worth approximately $3.4 trillion to $3.5 trillion.

Boards and advisers are reportedly discussing the terms, including the exchange ratio for Tesla shareholders and the governance structure.

An announcement could still be delayed until early 2027.

Elon Musk, who leads both companies and is their largest shareholder, has previously described a merger as a good idea, citing potential synergies in AI, chip design, robotics and orbital computing.

However, significant hurdles remain.

Tesla's China business, which accounts for roughly 20% of its revenue and a larger share of its earnings and free cash flow, could complicate the transaction.

JPMorgan has identified Chinese regulatory approval as the biggest obstacle.

Any deal would also require clearances across multiple jurisdictions and approval from Tesla shareholders, while the special committees overseeing discussions must demonstrate that their decisions serve shareholders' interests.

data.title: Nvidia stock outlook: Can shares recover after Jensen Huang's exit?
data.description:
Nvidia shares NVDA remained under pressure on Friday, falling 2.17% at the time of writing after recovering from an intraday decline of 4.6%.

The latest losses followed a 4.3% drop on Thursday after founder and longtime CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid reports concerning his personal relationships.

The departure has raised questions about Nvidia's leadership succession, corporate culture and exposure to potential regulatory scrutiny.

The company is also on track for its largest weekly market capitalisation decline on record.

However, analysts remain divided on the stock's outlook, with some arguing that its valuation offers an attractive entry point while others warn that the controversy could create longer-term risks.

Nvidia valuation and earnings could support a recovery

Despite the recent selloff, Nvidia shares trade at less than 12 times estimated earnings for the next 12 months, according to Barron's analysis.

A modest improvement in its valuation multiple could therefore support a significant recovery.

The company's upcoming third-quarter earnings report on Tuesday could provide an important catalyst.

Investors will closely monitor whether Nvidia reiterates its forecast for 70% revenue growth in fiscal 2028.

Any confirmation could help restore confidence in its growth prospects.

Additional share buybacks could also support the stock if its valuation remains depressed.

XTB analyst Kathleen Brooks said Nvidia's upcoming results would be closely watched following Huang's resignation.

While Brooks expects another strong earnings report, with revenue potentially exceeding the $108 billion estimate, she said the company's forward guidance would be more important for determining the stock's direction.

Yorkville Ives also maintained a bullish view, arguing that Nvidia remains the clear leader in GPU chips for the AI industry, with an estimated two-to-three-year advantage over its nearest competitor.

The analysts believe the current valuation does not fully reflect the company's position and see Colette Kress as a credible leader during the transition.

Leadership uncertainty remains an overhang

The absence of an immediate permanent successor is another challenge for Nvidia shares.

Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress is viewed as a potential interim leader, although the company is expected to require technical leadership for its next phase of growth.

Potential successors mentioned in early speculation include Ian Buck, Nvidia's vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing, and Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas.

Yorkville Ives also identified Apple CEO Tim Cook as a possible outside candidate, describing him as a dark-horse option given Nvidia's importance to the broader US technology industry.

A clearer succession plan or announcement of a shortlist could help reduce uncertainty surrounding the company's future direction.

Morgan Stanley reiterated its overweight rating on Nvidia but lowered its price target to $267 from $300.

The firm acknowledged that Huang's resignation, the absence of an immediate permanent successor and China-related regulatory risks represent setbacks.

However, it maintained that Nvidia's underlying business remains strong and that the risk-reward profile is attractive even under more conservative assumptions.

China scrutiny and corporate culture pose risks

The biggest threat to Nvidia's recovery could come from further developments surrounding the controversy that led to Huang's departure.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent questioned on Friday whether Nvidia had a sufficiently robust system to prevent its chips from reaching China through intermediaries.

Speaking to CNBC, he said he expected the company's board to conduct a thorough investigation.

Huang has reportedly agreed to testify before Congress, where lawmakers are interested in determining whether his reported relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence agent resulted in the transfer of intellectual property or advanced hardware to China.

Hendi Susanto, portfolio manager at Gabelli Funds, said the next developments could depend on the findings of investigations and the level of scrutiny from Washington, particularly concerning China and export controls.

Truist also downgraded Nvidia to hold from buy, citing concerns about the company's culture and the possibility that GPUs may have reached Chinese companies and government entities.

These concerns could affect future revenue prospects if they lead to tighter restrictions or additional regulatory action.

data.title: AMD falls 9%, Intel drops 6% as chip stocks slide on Friday
data.description:
AMD and Intel shares fell sharply on Friday as technology stocks came under pressure, with investors assessing inflation data and uncertainty surrounding Nvidia's leadership.

AMD shares plunged more than 9%, while Intel declined around 6%.

Nvidia shares also dropped 3%, contributing to broader market losses.

The S&P 500 fell around 0.73%, while the Nasdaq Composite declined over 1.2%.

Despite the selloff, analysts remain constructive on AMD's competitive position in the artificial intelligence (AI) chip market, pointing to its growing product portfolio, expanding data-center business and opportunities arising from Nvidia's leadership uncertainty.

Inflation data initially lifts equities before reversal

US equities initially moved higher after October's producer price index (PPI) report showed wholesale prices increasing 0.3% month over month, below the 0.4% increase expected by economists polled by Dow Jones.

However, the report also showed producer prices rising 6.5% year over year, marking the largest annual increase since November 2022.

The inflation figures added to an uncertain backdrop for technology stocks, which subsequently reversed their initial gains.

Nvidia's leadership uncertainty also remained in focus following reports surrounding the potential departure of CEO Jensen Huang.

The development raises questions about the company's strategic investments, including its $5 billion investment in Intel in September 2025.

Nvidia formed a partnership with Intel to integrate the latter's central processing units (CPUs) with its own graphics processing units (GPUs).

Based on Intel's Thursday closing price of $61.20, Nvidia's investment is now worth more than $13.14 billion.

Although the investment has generated substantial gains, Nvidia is not under immediate pressure to sell its stake.

A potential divestment could also attract scrutiny from the Trump administration, which views Intel as an important player in US semiconductor manufacturing.

Recent analyst calls on the company have been mixed. Bank of America, RBC Capital and Barclays all kept hold ratings on the stock in recent updates.

Bank of America slashed its target price from $100 to $80.

Analysts see AMD gaining ground against Nvidia

Despite AMD's share price decline, Seaport Research analyst Jay Goldberg sees the company as an increasingly credible competitor to Nvidia.

Speaking to CNBC on Friday, Goldberg said AMD now offers "formidable products" that compete more effectively with Nvidia.

Goldberg believes uncertainty surrounding Nvidia could accelerate efforts by customers to diversify their chip suppliers.

While he stopped short of suggesting that Nvidia had lost its dominant position, he argued that AMD had progressed beyond simply establishing a foothold in the market.

Prime Capital Financial CIO Will McGough also sees opportunities for AMD and Broadcom as Nvidia navigates its leadership transition.

Speaking to CNBC on Friday, McGough highlighted Anthropic's use of AMD chips and said the market was reassessing Nvidia's competitive advantage as alternative suppliers improve their offerings.

He also pointed to Alphabet's Google, Amazon, and Chinese chipmakers developing their own silicon, potentially creating additional competition for Nvidia while opening opportunities for AMD.

Data-center growth could support AMD's expansion

Counterpoint Research's latest analysis also highlighted AMD's growing position in the data-center market.

Counterpoint expects the data center segment to contribute more than 80% of AMD's revenue in 2027, with estimated data-center revenue reaching approximately $77 billion.

The firm also noted that AMD's fourth-quarter revenue guidance of around $17 billion was approximately $800 million above consensus estimates.

Data-center revenue is expected to increase around 50% sequentially.

Counterpoint expects AMD's server business to roughly double in 2027, while AI-related data-center revenue could more than double.

The research firm said AMD's current advantage over Intel in data centers primarily comes from AI GPUs and racks rather than CPUs.

However, it expects meaningful gains in x86 server market share in 2027.

AMD has also secured supply from Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company to support its projected expansion.

data.title: Why are Micron, SK Hynix, and SanDisk stocks falling on Friday?
data.description:
Memory stocks including Micron, SK Hynix and SanDisk suffered losses on Friday as continued weakness in Nvidia weighed on semiconductor shares and intensified concerns about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence trade.

Micron MU and SK Hynix fell around 5% each, while SanDisk plunged 8%.

Nvidia slipped more than 4%, dragging the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down over 5%.

The losses were considerably steeper than those in the broader market, with the Nasdaq falling 1.4% and the S&P 500 losing nearly 0.8%.

The selloff came even as October's producer price index (PPI) data came in softer than expected.

However, headline PPI accelerated 6.5% annually, up 0.2 percentage points and marking its highest annual rate since November 2022.

Nvidia uncertainty spills over into memory stocks

The turmoil surrounding Nvidia has raised questions about the broader AI trade, given the chipmaker's central role in the industry's expansion and its financial relationships with several companies across the ecosystem.

Investors are increasingly weighing concerns about AI infrastructure spending, debt financing, and the returns on massive capital investments.

Prolonged uncertainty around Nvidia could put additional pressure on valuations across the semiconductor sector.

China adds another layer of uncertainty.

Tighter US restrictions on advanced chips could accelerate domestic semiconductor substitution while making it harder for Chinese cloud companies to access sophisticated computing technology.

Memory stocks were already under pressure before Friday's decline.

Micron has lost around 21% over the past month, while SK Hynix is down approximately 18%.

The stocks also suffered a sell-off following Democratic victories in both houses of Congress, amid concerns that the political outcome could slow data centre construction across the US.

According to Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo, further trouble at Nvidia could particularly affect SK Hynix and Micron.

SK Hynix's leading position as a supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for Nvidia leaves it exposed to potential disruptions in the chipmaker's product roadmap.

However, demand for advanced memory from other AI platforms could remain strong, providing some support to the stock.

For Micron, Nvidia-related delays could affect near-term demand expectations for advanced memory.

Nevertheless, competing AI accelerator platforms also require high-performance memory, which could help cushion the impact.

SanDisk faces additional NAND pricing concerns

SanDisk suffered a steeper decline, with shares falling 8% on Friday and losing more than 42% over the past month.

The latest pressure followed a warning from Kioxia about a potential surge in NAND flash prices, raising fresh questions about competitive pricing dynamics and the sustainability of SanDisk's elevated gross margins.

Also, the company's data centre business, which generated the bulk of its recent revenue growth, is heavily dependent on AI infrastructure spending linked to Nvidia's GPU ecosystem.

Any perceived threat to Nvidia's strategic continuity could therefore translate into uncertainty over future NAND flash demand.

However, Evercore ISI remains optimistic about SanDisk's longer-term prospects.

The brokerage reiterated its Outperform rating and $2,500 price target on Wednesday, arguing that investors are underestimating structural changes in the memory chipmaker's business.

The firm held investor meetings with CEO David Goeckeler and head of investor relations Ivan Donaldson over the past two days.

“We think investors remain overly focused on how long NAND pricing can stay elevated rather than appreciating the structural changes to SNDK’s model,” Evercore wrote.

Management sees a changing NAND market in which suppliers manage output to match demand rather than simply maximise production.

Price increases have now lasted around six quarters, compared with roughly two quarters historically.

Gross margins above 80% also reduce suppliers' incentive to chase market share.

Evercore believes SanDisk's multi-year supply agreements, which include committed demand, price floors and ceilings, and financial guarantees, could limit downside risks during a future downturn.

The brokerage also said data centre demand remained robust, with customers seeking additional supply for AI systems being deployed now.

A shift towards more durable, specialised memory could further tighten industry supply.

“NBMs + supply discipline should support more durable profitability, while AI demand + HBF provide incremental growth opportunities,” the firm said.

data.title: Analyst who warned about Nvidia and Jensen Huang flagged Ethereum price
data.description:
Ethereum price has intensified its sell-off today, reaching its lowest level since August 19 this year. It has now slumped by over 31.5% from its highest point in August this year, and technicals suggest that it has more downside to go. For one, Culper Research, the research shop that warned about Jensen Huang affair also warned about Ethereum. 

Culper Research warned about Ethereum

Jensen Huang made headlines this week after confirming that he had an affair with a Chinese national whom US intelligence officials believe to be a spy. The report led to his resignation on Thursday.

While the report has shocked Wall Street, it was nothing new to Culper Research, a New York firm that warned about the affair with Alice Huang in May.

Investors have now turned their attention to Culper’s other warnings, including one it issued against Ethereum in March. At the time, the firm said it was short Ethereum, the second-biggest cryptocurrency in the world. It also disclosed a short position on BitMine, the biggest Ethereum holder in the world.

In its report on Ethereum, Culper Research said that Ethereum was in a “death spiral” after last year’s Fusaka upgrade. One of the aspects is that base fees collected on Ethereum will continue falling, meaning that less ETH is burned under EIP-1559. As a result, that means that Ethereum’s deflationary story will keep weakening.

This view has been confirmed by the recent data by DeFi Llama. The numbers show that Ethereum has generated just $27.3 million in fees this quarter, down from $34 million in the previous quarter. In total, the chain has made $153 million this year, down from $523 million last year.

Further, while Ethereum wallet growth has intensified, Culper Research found that most of this was because of spam. Indeed, the analyst found that 22% of all Ethereum transactions were tied to address poisoning. 

The analyst also warned that Vitalik Buterin had continuing selling his ETH coins, a sign that he expects the coin to remain under pressure. 

Ethereum ETF outflows have soared

Fundamentals also explain why ETH price has continued falling. Data shows that spot Ethereum ETF outflows have surged in the past few weeks. They have lost over $766 million this month after losing $1.6 billion last month. In total, they have lost over $2.6 billion in this period, a sign that demand has continued to wane.

More data shows that Ethereum’s futures open interest has continued to fall. The daily figure dropped by 6.5% in the last 24 hours to $23.5 billion. At its peak this year, Ethereum had an open interest of over $60 billion. A falling open interest is a sign that investors expect the coin to continue dropping. 

Ethereum liquidations have jumped in the past few months as exchanges closed leveraged positions, leading to more pressure.

ETH price technical analysis

Ethereum price chart | Source: TradingView

Technicals suggest that ETH price has more downside to go. It is about to form a death cross pattern as the spread between the 50-day and 200-day moving averages narrowed. This death cross pattern normally points to more downside.

The coin has dropped below the 61.8% Fibonacci Retracement level, confirming more downside. Therefore, the path of the least resistance for the token is bearish, with the next target to watch being at $1,500. On the flip side, a move above the 50% retracement level of $2,157 will invalidate the bearish outlook.
